comments.text:
Thanks, but does this actually work? You have used `vapply()` without `FUN.VALUE`, which gives me an error.

I'm testing a version where the conversion is done in `utils:::findMatches()` rather than `specialCompletions()`.

```
findMatches <- function(pattern, values)
{
    comps <- 
        if (.CompletionEnv$settings[["fuzzy"]])
            findFuzzyMatches(pattern, values)
        else
            findExactMatches(pattern, values)
    if (length(comps) && all(nzchar(comps)))
        comps <- vapply(comps,
                        FUN = function(comp) deparse1(as.name(comp), backtick = TRUE),
                        FUN.VALUE = "")
}
```

Hopefully this will work in more situations (though the only nontrivial example I've found so far is `?mostattri[TAB]`.

The problem is that with

```
x = list("abc+def" = 1, "def-abc" = 2, "abc-def" = 3)
```

both `x$[TAB]` and `x$a[TAB]` are pretty much useless. To fix this, we need to undo the backtick somehow (which may depend on the backend).

But I'm more worried that with

```
x = list("abc+def" = 1, "def-abc" = 2, "abc-def" = 3, defabc = 4)
```

`x$def[TAB]`, which actually deletes the 'def' part, and  at least for readline, I have no idea how to prevent that from happening.

Anyway, this is a good start. I will take a closer look when I get a chance, but meanwhile more testing + patches are welcome.

Thanks Deepayan. See the latest on the GitHub PR for a patch that includes tests and moves the logic into `findMatches()`.

I'll update the patch here once it's passing CI there.

I'm not sure I follow your point about the case with arithmetic names. I added your example as a test case -- I think the suggestions from the current revision are good.

Oh, I see, `deparse1()` doesn't know what to do with `as.name("abc-def")`. That sort of seems like a `deparse()` bug to ignore `typeof()` being "name" like that.

`print(as.name("abc-def"))` gives the backticks just fine, but neither `format()` nor `as.character()` do the right thing here for `name` input.

Spoke too soon -- the issue was with `ls()` being used for the `.DollarNames.environment` branch & skipping the new `deparse1()` logic. Updated the PR.

(PS as near as I can tell, `print()` is indeed just using `deparse` to get the backticks: https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/a33b9daf0dadc793addeba4c4ce41964280e245d/src/main/print.c#L872-L877)

comments.text:
What are the backends you care about?

Here is the issue in more detail.

Consider

```
y = as.list(1:11)
names(y) = month.name[-1]
veryLongVariableWithOneSuffix <- 1
veryLongVariableWithDifferentSuffix <- 2
```

What should happen for ambiguous completions? E.g.,

```
y$J[TAB]
```

or

```
veryLongVar[TAB]
```

The choices are to complete to a minimal common prefix, or just list everything.

RStudio just lists everything in a pop-up, and then if you insist by pressing TAB again, it just picks one from the list (probably the first one). ESS+company also does the same thing (probably the last). 

I think picking one item arbitrarily is not good, but it's not that big an issue if you provide a pop-up list first.

Unfortunately, readline has no option to give a pop-up menu to choose from, so it's much more natural to complete to a minimum common prefix.

Unfortunately, if you now add

```
y$`June 2` <- 13
```

your possible completions of `y$Ju` now look like 

```
> rc.status()$comps
[1] "y$June"     "y$July"     "y$`June 2`"
```

and the minimum common prefix is nothing.

To see a more serious effect of this, run R with your patch and try

```
?clas[TAB]
```

Now, ESS+company will probably still be OK, and your patch is a useful addition there. 

But ESS with default Emacs completion will discard the backticks, I think (because it doesn't start with what it thinks is the prefix), and Rgui on Windows can't modify the prefix either (that's another long-pending fix). I have to check the Mac GUI. So the major target here is probably readline, right?

But if a change causes major usability problems with readline, as your current patch does, there's not much point in doing it unless we can figure out how to fix it.

I will not be able to take a closer look before next week at the earliest.

Thanks for the added context Deepayan!

finally answering my question on why this hasn't been done before :)

comments.text:
Hmm, even though this is a `Confirmed` bug,  I'm not sure that it should be fixed.  As we see in your discussion, a "fix" might lead to completion code that's considerably more complicated .. needing much more resources to maintain, etc.

To put it short: People who use spaces in variable names *should* notice that it is almost always a bad idea, and should rather do sum `gsub()` fiddling to replace all spaces either by nothing or by `"_"`  or whatever is appropriate.
comments.creator: maechler
michaelchirico4
comments.text:
My current sense from Deepayan's comment is that it's up to the consumer of the suggested completions to wrap backticks if needed. One enhancement could be a new piece of metadata flagging non-syntactic completions to make it easier for downstreams to handle back-ticking if needed.

(I do think the R REPL could do that without running into the risks Deepayan described; whether it's "worth it" is a more open question.)

Some more context: this is started from just such a downstream consumer of the suggested completions: IRkernel (the main source of support for R in Jupyter / Colab notebooks):

https://github.com/IRkernel/IRkernel/issues/733

In sum, they have some messy clean-up logic for detecting non-syntactic names that's buggy / a bit fragile. I was hoping to solve this issue in R itself and free them from maintaining duplicate-ish logic for completions.

comments.creator: deepayan.sarkar
comments.text: Thanks for the context. This sounds like a very legitimate use, so I would like to come up with a workable solution. One obvious choice is to control this using a setting that IRkernel can activate, but maybe we could do better.
